text:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: Incident created — GPU capacity exhaustion / driver errors in us-west-2 (sev2). Paging oncall. Thread started at 2026-03-14T09:12:03Z

alice: getting alerts: queue depth spiking on inference-frontend, throttles across multiple pools. logs show CUDA Xid 57 and kernel OOM on several nodes.

sam: on it. which pool? dedicated-usw2-gpu-pool-1 and burst-pool-usw2. latency is up ~3x, 429s seen.

maria: customer impact: several Dedicated customers in us-west-2 seeing timeouts and failed requests; CS already fielding tickets.

devon: grabbing k8s events now. looks like nodes are flapping: kubelet restarting, driver pods crashing with exit code 137 (OOM).

alice: logs snippet: ```
2026-03-14T09:10:50Z driver[pid=2314]: cuda:xid=57: GPU page fault during kernel launch
2026-03-14T09:11:12Z kubelet: eviction: memory.available low
2026-03-14T09:11:19Z runtime: process killed by OOM
```

kyle: autoscaler report: tried to scale out but hit account quota and then failed to attach more GPUs; scale events show LB drain backlog. scale_min set to 2, scale_max 20, current desired 20 but only 14 active due to node registration errors.

lisa: @sam please confirm if this is isolated to driver 515.86 rollout? We did a gradual rollout yesterday.

sam: yes, can confirm 515.86 driver pods show higher crash counts on nodes with >32GB GPU memory. rollback might be necessary.

devon: let's reduce load first. Suggest switching user-facing traffic to fallback model variant (cpu/light) for affected tenants while we stabilize. Can we flip routing?

alice: initiating canary failover policy: route=cost:prefer-fallback for route group "inference-prod-usw2". Will take ~30s to propagate.

incidentbot: Routing change applied by alice at 2026-03-14T09:18:02Z — traffic shift started.

maria: FYI CS: sending templated update to impacted customers: "We are experiencing elevated errors in us-west-2; routing to fallback models in progress. Further updates in 30m."

kyle: infra note: nodes failing to register due to driver crash loop prevents autoscaler from increasing capacity even though quotas theoretically allow attach. Need to fix driver or revert.

sam: I'm going to rollback driver to 515.76 on a subset. Plan: cordon 3 nodes, drain, update driver daemonset to 515.76, uncordon. Will run as canary.

devon: put a hold on autoscaler for a bit: setting scale_disabled=true for the cluster to avoid churning while we roll.

lisa: commands I ran to cordon/drain (example): ```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-07 -n inference
kubectl drain gpu-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n inference
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/gpu-driver -n kube-system
```

sam: starting rollback on gpu-node-07-09 now. watching driver pods.

alice: handoff: @sam I'm going offline in 20m to take APM call. @devon you'll take oncall after that.

sam: acknowledged. I'll document steps in the incident channel and escalate to hardware if driver rollback doesn't stabilize within 15m.

incidentbot: oncall handover scheduled: from alice -> devon at 2026-03-14T09:32:00Z.

devon: noticed one node failed to unmount GPU device: ``error: device busy`` during drain. I restarted kubelet and retried, drain completed. Driver pod on gpu-node-07 is now stable on 515.76.

kyle: telemetry: after routing change, tail latency for affected routes dropped from p95 2.1s -> 0.6s, request success rate improved to 93% from 54%. Good.

maria: CS update: sent second message: "Routing to fallback model is reducing error rate, we're rolling back a recent driver update and expect further improvements shortly."

sam: rolling back daemonset cluster-wide in 3 batches to avoid mass restarts. Batching by AZ: batch size 4.

devon: watchlist: watch for Xid 31/57 reappearing, kernel OOMs, and node flaps. If Xid continues, we'll open driver bug with vendor and consider immediate pool-level capacity limits to prevent hot-shredding workloads.

alice: any customers with dedicated reserved capacity — they may still see throttles if their pools lost nodes. @maria can you compile a list of 10-highest impacted tenants?

maria: sending list to incident thread DM; will attach ticket links.

kyle: autoscaler: I've bumped scale_max to 30 as a temporary quota request is pending, but new nodes won't help until driver stays up. Also temporary manual add of 4 nodes in us-west-2 requested via cloud console (provisioning).

sam: after first batch rollback, driver crash loops dropped 90%. We're seeing nodes come back to Ready. Continuing to next batch.

devon: I'm taking over oncall now. @alice thanks, enjoy your call. I'll coordinate next updates and timeline to resolution.

incidentbot: Timeline note appended by devon at 2026-03-14T09:44:05Z: "Rollbacks in progress; routing mitigations active; customer impact reduced; monitoring for recurrence."

maria: CS: pushing status update to customers: ETA for full recovery 45-60m, will post earlier if stable.

devon: next steps: complete rollback across remaining nodes, monitor GPU OOM/Xid rate for 30m, unblock autoscaler, deprecate 515.86 rollout and draft PR to stop further rollouts until root cause triaged. If stable, revert routing to primary traffic.

kyle: provisioning additional nodes completed (4), but they'll be held out of scale group until we confirm driver stability.

sam: closing loop: after full rollback and 40m of clean telemetry, we'll mark incident as mitigated. Will escalate to research team for driver analysis and to vendor for Xid signatures if we see reoccurrence.

incidentbot: Incident severity downgraded to sev3 at 2026-03-14T10:20:45Z by devon. Final note: "Customers observed reduced errors; root cause suspected driver regression in 515.86; follow-up required."

lisa: adding a follow-up task: postmortem owner = sam. Target publish in 48h.

maria: confirmed CS follow-up plan and outreach timeline.

devon: handover to next oncall scheduled in 6h. Leaving runbook links and commands in thread.

alice: back from call — good work team.

sam: thanks all.
